To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a transposable element was identified in a gene involved in the transfer/dilution effect and the transposable element insertion into the gene is responsible for the variation in the transfer/dilation effect.
the insertion of a transposon in a gene can be a cause of somaclonal variation in cultured cells.
the insertion of a new transposable element in one cell of a cell culture line during repeated subculturing can lead to the appearance of somaclonal variation in the cell line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the somaclonal variation of cultured cells of carrot (Daucus carota L.) that was caused by the insertion of a transposon, Tdc1.
the following questions: (1) What are the molecular mechanisms underlying the variation in plant cells?
the following questions: (1) How can a transposable element insert into a gene in plant cells that are maintained for many years in culture?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tdc1 is an En/Spm-like element that is inserted into a PAL gene and that the insertion of Tdc1 into gDcPAl1 causes a reduction in PAL gene expression.
the transposable element insertion into a PAL gene caused somaclonal variation in the cell culture.
the Tdc1 element was mobilized in one or a few cells during the first 5 years of the culture, that this cell(s) became established and that Tdc1 was transmitted clonally to all of its descendants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Tdc1 transposable element was activated in a plant cell and inserted into the gDCPAL1 gene.
a transposable element can cause a somatic variant in plant cell cultures.
the Tdc1 insertion occurred during subculturing of a cell line that had been established from a single cell, but that the insertion event did not cause the cell line to disappear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transposable elements, which are present in most plants, are a major source of variation in plant cell cultures.
the use of long-term subcultured cell lines for genetic studies can be misleading and that it is important to use cell lines that are as close to the original plant as possible.

transposons can be a source of variation in plant cell cultures, and that the presence of transposons in plant genomes should be considered when analyzing the molecular basis of phenotypic variation in cell culture lines.
